# Eric Wan saddened by "My Date with a Vampire" director's death

Heidi Hsia

1 min read

Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

16 Jul - ATV actor Eric Wan recently expressed his sadness over the passing of director Billy Tang, who passed away earlier this month. [...] As reported on Mingpao, Eric, who worked with Billy in the hit drama, "My Date with a Vampire", was recently seen at the funeral of the said director before the body was cremated at Cape Collinson, saying that he wanted to bid Billy his last farewell.

"Billy was a good director. People who didn't really know him would have been surprised to find that he really liked to laugh. He laughed a lot," he said.

Talking about Billy's condition prior to his death, Eric stated that the director was battling throat cancer and was told by the doctor that he would only last four to five years. However, he persisted for seven to eight years.

"I once told him not to keep working, but he said that he was happier when he was working," he added.

Eric also admitted that he remained in contact with Billy throughout the last months of his life, and that the director left surrounded by his family.

Dr. Wan’s research areas include machine learning, statistical signal processing, and health related technologies. He is currently the Director of the Biomedical Signal Processing Lab in the ECE Department. He is also an Adjunct Associate Professor in the Biomedical Engineering Department, Oregon Health & Science University. Dr. Wan has led a diverse number of research projects over the years ranging from autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles, speech enhancement for cellular communications, to [...] communications, to noninvasive glucose monitoring. Dr. Wan is best known for his pioneering work on the Unscented and Sigma-Point Kalman filters for probabilistic inference. Dr. Wan holds several patents in adaptive signal processing and integrated navigation and has authored over 90 technical papers in the field.
